A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ABBA research despite the changed title and formatting. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model fine-tuning results, matrix reconstruction experiments, an MNIST experiment, ablations, and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results in Tables 1–9 and Figures 1–4, including benchmark evaluations, ablations, and efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The Hadamard product of two learnable low-rank updates, SVD/LoRA initialization, scaling formula, Khatri–Rao implementation, and inference merging are retained. v3's expression as two rank-stabilized LoRA adapters restates mathematics already present in v1 Appendix D.2.

E1.justification: Both use COMMONSENSE170K and its eight evaluation tasks, MetaMathQA with GSM8K and MATH evaluation, the MNIST adaptation scenario, and the same matrix reconstruction scenarios. The changed MetaMathQA sample count affects experimental settings, not coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain full fine-tuning, LoRA, rsLoRA, PiSSA, DoRA, LoRA-Pro, and HiRA. The comparator sets in the MNIST, reconstruction, memory, and training-time comparisons also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 changes the reported MetaMathQA training subset from 50K to 20K examples for both arithmetic models, a substantial training-budget revision. Tables 4 and 7 also replace alpha values 8√2, 16√2, and 32√2 with 12, 24, and 48. The PDFs do not establish whether these changes correct reporting or reflect reruns.

E4.justification: The documented scaling-sensitivity analyses in Tables 4 and 7 associate retained accuracy rows with several revised alpha settings. This is a limited revision to the reported sensitivity evidence. Initialization, adapter placement, rank allocation, total-rank, and adapter-chain analyses otherwise retain the same comparisons and outcomes.

E5.justification: Appendix H in both versions reports mean performance over three random seeds. Neither adds confidence intervals, standard deviations, significance tests, or a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Reported accuracy and training-time values in Tables 1–9 and all plotted outcomes remain unchanged. For example, Mistral-7B ABBA at rank 32 retains 66.26 on GSM8K and 18.08 on MATH. The revised setting descriptions do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: v3 removes v1's probabilistic superiority theorem, Hadamard-manifold definition, and Appendix D.3 proof. It replaces the effective-scaling and initialization-stability theorems with a theorem asserting necessary and sufficient rank scaling under independent, mean-zero random-matrix assumptions, with a revised Appendix D.2 proof. The Khatri–Rao theorem and initialization-gradient derivations remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the expressivity contribution from theoretical and empirical analysis to empirical reconstruction evidence. Claims about the architecture, parameter efficiency, computational efficiency, and benchmark superiority remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 removes Section 6's specific limitations concerning unevaluated ViTs/VLMs, concurrent adapter-serving costs, and untested adapter merging. Section 3.2 adds a hypothesis that implicit regularization explains performance exceeding full fine-tuning. Other interpretations, including rank saturation and chained-adapter instability, remain.

D1.justification: Tables 4 and 7 revise the scaling-hyperparameter documentation, replacing paired effective-scale/alpha entries with revised alpha-only entries; the conversion formula remains available. Appendix H and Table 10 retain the software, hardware, precision, optimizer, and other training details. The stated code-access location is unchanged.

R1.justification: The distinct cited works and substantive positioning relative to LoRA, HiRA, and structured adaptation remain unchanged. v3 consolidates duplicate LoRA-GA references and updates reference ordering and bibliographic metadata; these do not add or remove distinct prior work.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title and headings, consolidates the scaling discussion, makes localized abstract and initialization-description edits, and adds Appendix J's writing-assistance disclosure. Most prose and the main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: All four figures and ten tables are retained, with identical figure graphics. v3 changes the document template and headers, relocates tables within the text, numbers initialization rows, and revises scaling-table columns and captions. These are limited presentation changes.

improvement.justification: v3 improves claim calibration: it withdraws the probabilistic expressivity guarantee and removes v1's argument that zero output moments satisfy a Θ(1) stability requirement. However, it deletes substantive applicability and deployment limitations, while changing training counts and scaling settings without explaining the unchanged scores. The PDFs do not resolve whether those protocol edits improve reporting accuracy or introduce inconsistencies, so a reliable net quality judgment is not possible.
